full_judgment:
6. The suit was contested by defendant No. 1 Md. Selim (appellant No. 1 of Civil Appeal No. 500 of 2009) by filing written statement in one set and defendant Nos. 4- 10 other heirs of Mustafizur Rahman (appellants Nos. 2-6 and respondent No. 2 respectively of Civil Appeal No. 500 of 2008) by filing another set of written statement. Both sets of defendants denied the material allegations made in the plaint stating inter-alia that they instituted Other Class Suit No. 54 of 1984 (originally Other Class Suit No. 264 of 1984) in the Court of Assistant Judge, Lohagara, against Ismail Sowdagor and others for declaration of their title in respect of the self same suit property and further declaration that by registered deed No. 826 dated 17.02.1982, allegedly executed by Ashab Mia, the defendant No. 1 (Md. Ismail Sowdagar) did not purchase the shop room and as such the said Ismail Sowdagar did not get the shop by purchase. Subsequently the plaintiff amended some of the paragraphs of the plaint along with the prayer and added the prayer for eviction of the defendant No. 1, Md. Ismail Sowdagar from the suit land. So the suit was a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession upon eviction of defendant No. 1. 

 29. One thing is to be kept in mind that two suits, one filed by Ismail Sowdagar for title and partition and the other, filed by Md. Selim and others initially for declaration and subsequently by amendment for declaration and eviction and recovery of khas possession. The subject matter of two suits are completely different. It is not denied by Ismail Sowdagar (the present respondent No. 1) that he entered into the suit shop as a tenant. The P.Ws. as well as the D.Ws. and defendant No. 25, Hafeza Khatun, all have admitted that Ismail Sowdagar is a tenant under Md. Selim and others. If the tenancy is proved the only question remains whether he is an ejectable tenant for non-payment of rent and/or when the tenant upon disowning the title of the landlord, claims himself to be the owner. Both the Courts below specifically disbelieved the sale deed executed by Ashab Miah to Ismail Showdagor as the plot number described in the schedule of the sale deed (Exhts 1 and 2 ) do not tally with Ashab Miah's deed of purchase from Mustafiz the predecessor of Md. Selim and others. The khatian numbers stated therein do not contain the name of Ashab Miah or that of Ismail Showdagor rather the same contains the name of Mustafiz, the predecessor of Md. Selim and others. Again the suit land sold to Ashab Miah by Mostafizur Rahman in 1965 appears to be completely a separate plot under B.S. Khatian Nos. 551 and 82, Plot Nos. 6293 and 6295 whereas the suit plot is Plot No. 2353. So there is no reason to hold that Ismail Sowdagar purchased the suit plot from Ashab Miah as Ashab did not purchase the same from Mostafiz. When the vendor does not have any title on a property and if the same is transferred to the vendee no title is transferred by such deed to the vendee. Thus Ismail Sowdagar did not get any title in the suit land. The courts below concurrently found the same. But the High Court Division without consideration this aspect passed the impugned judgment and order which is not in accordance with law.
